Part of the analysis code for the matched liver–serum multi-omics study in MASLD. This script is self-contained: open it in RStudio (or `rmarkdown::render("Hepatic_lipidome.Rmd")` from this folder). It first loads the workspace of the previous step (`Fig1_hepatic_transcriptome`), running that script if needed. Input data are read from `data/` (see `data/README.md`); Supplementary Tables used here are in `Source_data/`; Source Data for this item are written to `Source_data/`; other outputs go to `results/`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE)
.root <- if (exists("REPO_ROOT")) REPO_ROOT else {
  d <- normalizePath(getwd())
  while (!file.exists(file.path(d, "common", "setup.R")) && dirname(d) != d) d <- dirname(d)
  d
}
source(file.path(.root, "common", "setup.R"))
```

```{r prereq, include=FALSE}

```

```{r paths-fig, include=FALSE}

```

# Hepatic lipidome: Table S3

Liver lipidomics (n = 211): POMA preprocessing (half-minimum imputation, log2, autoscaling) and limma adjusted for age, BMI and sex; FDR <= 0.10.

#### Read Input Data and Subsetting Based on Gender for Downstream Analysis

```{r hepaticl-01, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE}
# Load description data
description <- data.frame(readxl::read_excel(file.path(project_dir, "Analyisis/description.xlsx")))
rownames(description) <- description$Exposure
description <- description[, -2]
# Load exposures data
exposures <- data.frame(readxl::read_excel(file.path(project_dir, "Analyisis/exposures.xlsx")))
rownames(exposures) <- exposures$id
exposures <- exposures[, -1]
# Replace zeros with NA
exposures[exposures == 0] <- NA
# Align exposures with phenotypic data
common_rows <- intersect(rownames(exposures), rownames(phenotype))
exposures_reordered <- exposures[rownames(phenotype), , drop = FALSE]
exposures <- exposures_reordered
# Validate alignment
table(row.names(exposures) == row.names(phenotype))
# Modify description data for better labeling
description$ID <- paste0(description$Family, "_", row.names(description))
description$ID <- gsub("rowid_", "", description$ID)
description$ID <- gsub(" ", "_", description$ID)
# Update row names for exposures
exposures <- t(exposures)
new_row_names <- description$ID[match(rownames(exposures), rownames(description))]
rownames(exposures) <- new_row_names
exposures <- t(exposures)
lipidomics_exposures <- exposures
# Clean phenotype data
df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(phenotype, "SampleID")
min_value_GGT_UL <- min(df$GGT_UL, na.rm = TRUE)
df$GGT_UL[is.na(df$GGT_UL)] <- min_value_GGT_UL / 2
df$Menopause_YN <- NULL
```

#### Data Normalization and Visualization

```{r hepaticl-02, fig.align='center', fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
# Create a POMA object
data <- POMA::PomaCreateObject(metadata = df, features = exposures)
# Impute missing data using half-minimum method
imputed <- data %>%
  PomaImpute(method = "half_min", zeros_as_na = TRUE, remove_na = TRUE, cutoff = 20)
log2_transformed <- imputed %>%
    PomaNorm(method = "log_transform")
# Normalize the data using log scaling
normalized <- log2_transformed %>%
  PomaNorm(method = "auto_scaling")
# Create boxplots for visualization before and after normalization
a <- PomaBoxplots(imputed, x = "samples") +
     ggplot2::ggtitle("Not Normalized") +
     ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank())
b <- PomaBoxplots(log2_transformed, x = "samples") +
     ggplot2::ggtitle("Log transformed") +
     ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank())
c <- PomaBoxplots(normalized, x = "samples") +
    ggplot2::ggtitle("Auto scaling") +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank())
# Combine the plots for comparison
#a + b + c
b + c
```

```{r hepaticl-03, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide', fig.align='center', fig.width=8}
# Convert normalized data to a data frame
exposures_Normalized <- as.data.frame(normalized@assays@data@listData)
# Perform hierarchical clustering to detect outliers in metabolites
sampleTree <- hclust(dist(t(exposures_Normalized)), method = "average")
plot(sampleTree, main = "Metabolites (Lipidomics) Clustering to Detect Outliers",
     sub = "", xlab = "", cex.lab = 1.5, cex.axis = 1.5, cex.main = 2)
```

## Prepare covariates and sample alignment for limma (lipidome)

```{r hepaticl-04, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
df <- phenotype
df$Gender_M0F1 <- ifelse(df$Gender_M0F1 == "Male", 0, 1)
df$Steatosis <- ifelse(df$steatosis_Kleiner == 0, 0, 1)
df$Inflammation <- ifelse(df$inflammation_Kleiner == 0, 0, 1)
df$Fibrosis <- ifelse(df$fibrosis_Kleiner_04 == 0, 0, 1)
df$steatosis_Kleiner <- NULL; df$inflammation_Kleiner <- NULL; df$ballooning_Kleiner <- NULL
df$NASH_Kleiner_YN <- NULL; df$fibrosis_Kleiner_04 <- NULL; df$NAS_score <- NULL; df$Menopause_YN <- NULL
df <- df %>% dplyr::rename(Age = Age_yr, Gender = Gender_M0F1, BMI = BMI_kgm2, Glucose = Glucose_mgdL,
  HbA1c = HbA1c_percent, AST = AST_UL, ALT = ALT_UL, GGT = GGT_UL, Cholesterol = Cholesterol_mgdL,
  HDL = HDL_mgdL, LDL = LDL_mgdL, Triglycerides = TG_mgdL)
# align covariates with the normalised lipid matrix (features x samples)
common_samples <- intersect(colnames(exposures_Normalized), rownames(df))
df <- df[common_samples, ]
df$SampleID <- rownames(df)
```

#### DEGs Lipids

```{r hepaticl-05}
# Transpose matrix: rows = metabolites, columns = samples
metabo_mat <- (as.matrix(exposures_Normalized))
# Check dimensions
dim(metabo_mat)
# Should be: features x samples, e.g., 701 x 189
# Ensure column names match metadata rownames
all(colnames(metabo_mat) == (df$SampleID))  # should be TRUE
# Phenotype metadata
metadata <- df
metadata$Steatosis <- factor(metadata$Steatosis, levels = c(0,1))
metadata$Inflammation <- factor(metadata$Inflammation, levels = c(0,1))
metadata$Fibrosis <- factor(metadata$Fibrosis, levels = c(0,1))
metadata$Gender <- factor(metadata$Gender, levels = c(0,1))  # 0 = Male, 1 = Female
# Differential analysis function
run_diff <- function(phenotype){
  design <- model.matrix(~ Age + BMI + Gender + metadata[[phenotype]], data = metadata)

  fit <- lmFit(metabo_mat, design)
  fit <- eBayes(fit)

  # Coefficient of interest = last column (phenotype effect)
  coef_name <- ncol(design)
  res <- topTable(fit, coef = coef_name, number = Inf, adjust.method = "fdr")
  return(res)
}
# Run for each phenotype
res_steatosis <- run_diff("Steatosis")
res_inflammation <- run_diff("Inflammation")
res_fibrosis <- run_diff("Fibrosis")
# Filter significant metabolites (FDR ≤ 0.10)
sig_steatosis <- res_steatosis[res_steatosis$adj.P.Val <= 0.1, ]
sig_inflammation <- res_inflammation[res_inflammation$adj.P.Val <= 0.1, ]
sig_fibrosis <- res_fibrosis[res_fibrosis$adj.P.Val <= 0.1, ]
# Add phenotype and direction columns for each condition
sig_steatosis_tbl <- sig_steatosis %>%
  mutate(Phenotype = "Steatosis",
         Direction = ifelse(logFC > 0, "Up", "Down"),
         Metabolite = rownames(sig_steatosis)) %>%
  select(Metabolite, Phenotype, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, Direction)
sig_inflammation_tbl <- sig_inflammation %>%
  mutate(Phenotype = "Inflammation",
         Direction = ifelse(logFC > 0, "Up", "Down"),
         Metabolite = rownames(sig_inflammation)) %>%
  select(Metabolite, Phenotype, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, Direction)
sig_fibrosis_tbl <- sig_fibrosis %>%
  mutate(Phenotype = "Fibrosis",
         Direction = ifelse(logFC > 0, "Up", "Down"),
         Metabolite = rownames(sig_fibrosis)) %>%
  select(Metabolite, Phenotype, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, Direction)
# Combine all into a single table
combined_sig_tbl <- bind_rows(sig_steatosis_tbl, sig_inflammation_tbl, sig_fibrosis_tbl)
# Optional: sort by Phenotype and logFC
combined_sig_tbl <- combined_sig_tbl %>%
  arrange(Phenotype, desc(logFC))
# View table
write.csv(combined_sig_tbl, "Supplementary_Table_Significant_LIPIDS.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Plot summary for above result

```{r hepaticl-06}
# ---- 1. Phenotype-level summary ----
lipid_summary <- combined_sig_tbl %>%
  group_by(Phenotype, Direction) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
p1 <- ggplot(lipid_summary, aes(x = Phenotype, y = n, fill = Direction)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Up" = "#ffa500ff", "Down" = "#4575B4")) +
  labs(
    title = "Differential Lipids Across MASLD Histological Features",
    x = "Phenotype",
    y = "Number of Differential Lipids",
    fill = "Direction"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )
# ---- 2. Breakdown by lipid class ----
# Clean metabolite names to extract lipid class (before first "_")
combined_sig_tbl <- combined_sig_tbl %>%
  mutate(LipidClass = str_extract(Metabolite, "^[^_]+"))
lipid_class_summary <- combined_sig_tbl %>%
  group_by(Phenotype, LipidClass, Direction) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
lipid_class_summary$Phenotype <- factor(
  lipid_class_summary$Phenotype,
  levels = c("Steatosis", "Inflammation", "Fibrosis")
)
# Plot with correct order
p2 <- ggplot(lipid_class_summary, aes(x = LipidClass, y = n, fill = Direction)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Phenotype, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Up" = "#ffa500ff", "Down" = "#4575B4")) +
  labs(
    title = "Differential Lipids by Class Across MASLD Features",
    x = "Lipid Class",
    y = "Number of Differential Lipids",
    fill = "Direction"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold")
  )
# Print plots
p1
p2
```

## Table S3

```{r hepaticl-07, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
add_table("Table S3", combined_sig_tbl %>%
  dplyr::transmute(`Lipid main ID` = Metabolite, `Lipid Class` = LipidClass, Phenotype, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, Direction))
# NOTE: in the published table 'Lipid main ID' is the curated lipid name (e.g. TG(50:0)) and 'Lipid Class' the curated class;
# here the feature identifier of the lipid matrix is written to the first column.
```
